rule: The home club must reserve 10% of its seated tickets and 10% of its standing tickets for the away club until two weeks before the official match date, and away spectators may not be charged more than home spectators (DFB Durchführungsbestimmungen zur Spielordnung, § 25 no. 1).
note: Two press reports (2015, 2021, the second quoting the DFL) give the same 10% for away fans. A FLOOR, so may-add: a club may give more. The DFB's own rules for matches with increased risk list 'limiting ticket sales' as a measure, so at such a match the share can be cut (see risk-classification). appliesTo is unknown on purpose: the section speaks of 'Bundesspiele' and names the DFB-Pokal, the 3. Liga and the Lizenzligen, but which competitions count is defined in §§ 41-42 of the DFB-Spielordnung, which was not read. Read in the edition of 1 Feb 2023.

authority: DFB (Deutscher Fußball-Bund), after hearing the police
rule: A 'match with increased risk' is one where general experience or current information makes a particular danger sufficiently likely. The home club decides, as early as possible and after hearing the security bodies, above all the police commander, and must tell the DFB; the DFB may classify a match itself. Measures to be considered then include limiting ticket sales for standing and seated areas, strict separation of supporters with buffer blocks, and restrictions on alcohol.
note: DFB Richtlinien zur Verbesserung der Sicherheit bei Bundesspielen, § 32 (and the alcohol clause beside it), edition of 1 Feb 2023. ONE SOURCE - the DFB's own text; no second national source for the mechanism was read. implements: the scheme is national, but each home club classifies its own matches and chooses the measures, which is why the KSC derby rows say what was actually done (no alcohol in 2024-25). Press and police call the KSC-FCK derby a Hochrisikospiel (K21, K22, K23); that is a fixture fact and stays in club-ticket-rules.csv. appliesTo unknown for the reason given on the away-allocation row.

authority: DFL Deutsche Fußball Liga, with the clubs of the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga
rule: Under the nine fair-play rules the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs adopted with the league for the official ticket secondary market, a resold ticket may cost at most the club's original single-ticket price, and the service fee for the exchange may be at most 15% of the order value.
note: The league's page says the rules came in in 2015/16 and that the clubs that take part in the official secondary market guarantee them; it does not say every club takes part. KSC's own Zweitmarkt page says it follows these DFL rules (K14) - a club attributing the rule to the league, which is evidence about the league rule. implements: each club runs its own Zweitmarkt and writes its own resale terms, so a club row on resale-price-cap (Nürnberg's face value +10% for private handovers, KSC's ATGB +15%) is that club's implementation, not a contradiction. The two league Q-ids are from league-tiers.csv.
